description: I’m looking for teammates interested in frontend development, game mechanics, UI/UX or illustration, and space-science research. You don’t need to do everything. Bring one strength, communicate well, and help us make something we’re proud to demonstrate.
summary:
Storm Watch turns real NASA space-weather records into a mission young explorers can play. Designed for ages 7–12, this browser-based game puts players in charge of a Moon outpost facing an approaching particle storm. Across six turns, they balance power, oxygen, science collection and shelter preparation, preview consequences, and learn why preparation matters.

The experience connects 19 archived NASA DONKI records to an interactive evidence timeline that distinguishes observations, model forecasts and invented game rules. A changing lunar scene, three visual themes, keyboard controls and a mission debrief make complex decisions approachable.

Storm Watch addresses the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by making children active decision-makers rather than passive readers. Its goal is to build curiosity, systems thinking and an understanding of scientific uncertainty. It runs without an account or installation. The mission is educational fiction grounded in historical evidence, not a live forecast or real astronaut safety simulator.
details:
Storm Watch is a playable Moon-base mission built for young explorers aged 7–12. Players manage an outpost through six turns, choosing between three actions at each stage. Power, oxygen, science collection and shelter readiness interact, so a useful choice now can create a difficult trade-off later.

Before committing, players can preview resource changes. The illustrated outpost responds to mission state, while a debrief connects their choices to the outcome. Players can retry different strategies, save locally and resume later.
